Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

assume verb

take for granted

also take for granted, presume, I assume, take it that, assuming that

classical

Cic. Fam. 9.2.1: oblītum crēdidī

crēdō, crēdere, crēdidī, crēditum

verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive

assume, take it (that)

In conversation an assumption is simply what one believes or thinks: crēdō, putō (see believe, think).

Other words

  • pōnō, pōnere, posuī, positum — take it (that), lay down as given

    verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 165: pōnō satis in eō fuisse ōrātiōnis atque ingenī; Cic. Div. 1.118: hōc autem positō atque concessō

    Hōc positō: on this assumption. The imperative pōne, “suppose”, is late (Ambrose: Lewis & Short); for “suppose that …” see suppose.

  • sūmō, sūmere, sūmpsī, sūmptum — assume, take as granted (in an argument)

    verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.89: beātōs esse deōs sūmpsistī; Cic. Div. 2.104 (Lewis & Short)

  • prō certō habēre — take for granted, regard as certain

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.6.3 (Lewis & Short, s.v. habeō)

    See sure.

Examples

  • cōnscrīpsī epistulam noctū; nec ille ad mē rediit; oblītum crēdidī.

    I wrote the letter during the night; he never came back for it; I assumed he had forgotten.Cic. Fam. 9.2.1

  • Beātōs esse deōs sūmpsistī: concēdimus.

    You assumed that the gods are happy: we grant it.Cic. N.D. 1.89

  • tamen pōnō satis in eō fuisse ōrātiōnis atque ingenī

    yet I take it that he had eloquence and talent enoughCic. Brut. 165

  • Pōnō eum abīsse.

    I take it he has left.Traupman 93, who gives it for “I bet he has taken off” (see bet)

See also think, believe, suppose, sure.
